headline: Acadia Vehicle Reservations and Coastal Access
reservation: Acadia National Park requires a park entrance pass year-round. From May through October, Cadillac Summit Road requires a separate vehicle reservation, which must be booked online in advance. Coastal state parks and private ferries to Casco Bay islands operate on independent schedules; always verify the official NPS and Maine State Park sites for current seasonal changes.

days.title: Portland Waterfront and Headlights

stops.name: Old Port District
stops.detail: Walk the cobblestone streets and working waterfront to see the historic maritime architecture.

stops.name: Portland Head Light
stops.detail: Visit the iconic lighthouse at Fort Williams Park for coastal cliff walks and Atlantic views.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local Portland and Cape Elizabeth travel; traffic is heavy in July.
days.note: Parking at Fort Williams Park is limited; arrive early to secure a spot near the lighthouse.

days.title: Midcoast Harbors and Peninsulas

stops.name: Maine Maritime Museum
stops.detail: Explore the historic shipyard in Bath to understand the region's wooden boat-building heritage.

stops.name: Camden Hills State Park
stops.detail: Hike or drive to the summit of Mount Battie for a bird's-eye view of Camden Harbor.

days.driving: Allow 2.5-3 hours; Route 1 congestion is frequent through Wiscasset.
days.note: Coastal detours to peninsulas like Pemaquid Point add significant time; choose one major detour per day.

days.title: Mount Desert Island Exploration

stops.name: Ocean Path
stops.detail: Walk the scenic coastline from Sand Beach to Otter Cliff to see the granite formations.

stops.name: Jordan Pond
stops.detail: Follow the loop trail around the clear glacial water with views of the North and South Bubbles.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours from Camden to Bar Harbor; conditions vary by season.
days.note: Park Loop Road is one-way in many sections; plan your stops sequentially to avoid long loops.

days.title: Acadia Peaks and Carriage Roads

stops.name: Cadillac Mountain
stops.detail: Access the highest point on the US North Atlantic coast for expansive bay views.

stops.name: Eagle Lake Carriage Roads
stops.detail: Walk or cycle the motor-free gravel paths designed by Rockefeller for a quiet forest experience.

days.driving: Local island travel; allow 30-45 minutes for parking at popular trailheads.
days.note: Cadillac Mountain requires a timed vehicle reservation; check the NPS site for the 90-day and 2-day booking windows.

intel.title: Park Loop Road Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at Sand Beach and Jordan Pond often fill by 9 AM in summer. Utilize the Island Explorer shuttle to bypass parking bottlenecks.

intel.title: Island Provisioning
intel.text: Ellsworth is the last major town for standard grocery prices before crossing onto Mount Desert Island. Fuel is available in Bar Harbor but at a premium.

intel.title: Topographic Signal Loss
intel.text: Cell service is unreliable on the western side of Mount Desert Island and within deep valleys. Download the official NPS app for offline use.

intel.title: Seasonal Fog
intel.text: Dense coastal fog can appear suddenly, obscuring views at Cadillac Mountain and Pemaquid Point. Keep your itinerary flexible to swap viewpoints for museums.

intel.title: Coastal Town Constraints
intel.text: Camden and Bar Harbor have strictly enforced metered parking and residential zones. Use designated satellite lots and walk into the historic centers.

plan.arrival: Fly into Portland (PWM) or Bangor (BGR), pick up a rental car, and head to your first coastal base in Portland or Bar Harbor.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for the Maine coast; check for height restrictions if driving an RV on Acadia’s historic stone bridges.
plan.goldenHour: Bass Harbor Head Light is a popular sunset location, though parking is extremely limited and requires arriving well in advance.
